body.p: There lived a woman. She had three sons. The woman does all the housework: cooks food, sews clothes, crapes skins, stores water and firewood. And her sons go hunting. They kill wild reindeer, polar foxes, foxes. They also fish. They make nets, repair them, salt caviar, make dried fish. They install metal traps and wooden traps, they clean their rifles. The youngest brother was a good hunter and a good shooter. They always bring a lot of prey. They have a lot of things in their tent, a lot of meat, a lot of skins. So they live. One day in winter, their mother went for water. Her sons are waiting, but their mother will not come. They wait and wait, and then went to the ice hole themselves. They see, the buckets are at the edge of the ice hole, and their mother is absent. The lads cried, but no one was there. The youngest brother said. Probably, our mother has fallen into the ice hole. We should look for her under the water. The older sons said. If our mother really fell into the ice hole, how will we find her? The youngest brother said. Let's make a long rope. You two will hold the rope, and I will use it to go under the water. There I will look for my mother. The brothers tied together the ropes from the seine. It became a very long rope. The younger brother tied one end of the rope around himself. He gave the other end to his brothers for them to hold. He said to his brothers. I don't know how long I'll be walking there. Let one of you stand by the ice hole. When I pull the rope, drag it up. They let their younger brother go under the water. When he came under the water, he took off the rope and tied it to a tree. And himself he left. He goes and does not know himself where he is going. He goes and goes. Then a tent appeared in front of him, a huge copper tent. There is a lot of firewood lying near the tent. One pile of firewood is iron firewood, the other pile is copper firewood. He entered the tent. An old man and an old woman are lying on the bedding. And on the other half there is a girl, she is very beautiful. Whenever she moves, her metal jewelry rings. The old man said to the old woman: Old woman! A guest came to us from the tundra. He's probably tired and hungry. Light a fire, cook some meat.[ShA:] A non-possessive desinative form looks unexpected with no overt possessor. The old woman went outside. She brought iron firewood into the tent. She went out again and brought copper firewood in. He lit a fire. She hung her cauldron over the fire. The flame rises up. The copper tent glowed red hot. It became impossible to sit in it. Then the young man waved his left hand, and the fire became small. It barely reaches the bottom of the cauldron. The girl sits, looks at the young man and says nothing. The cauldron got boiled. They ate. Then they went to sleep. The young man lay down closer to the door. In the middle of the night, he heard a dog [ShA:] Unsure, maybe default class dÊ¼iminu- squealing near the door outdoors. He got up and went outside. Near the door of the tent he sawand thus dÊ¼iminuunuza. a small dog. The dog drags the young man behind itself by the tail of his outerwear. The young man went behind the dog. He saw tied sledges near the tent. The dog ran to one of the sledges [ShA:] Unsure, maybe default and squeaked quietly. The young man untied this sledge. And there his mother sits, alive and healthy.class dÊ¼iminu- and thus dÊ¼iminua. Only her eyes are red from crying. Seeing her son, she got happy. Then she said. Help me get out of here. But you can't do anything by force, you have to use cunning. After they spoke, her son tied the sledge again. He entered the tent. He entered the tent, but the girl was not on her bedding. He lay down and fell asleep. In the morning everyone got up and ate. The old man said. If you want to come back to the ground, take the little dog as your wife, taking any sledge as her dowry. The young man thought and didn't object. The old man collected his reindeer. The young man caught five bulls. He harnessed two bulls to the sledge in which his mother was sitting, and harnessed three of them to his own sledge. He took the little dog and left. His reindeer run quickly, there is no need to drive them. They reached the tree to which the rope was tied. He untied the rope from the tree, took his mother out of the sledge and pulled the rope. His brothers lifted their mother and pushed the rope back down. The second time they pulled out their brother with his dog. After they got to the ground, the dog jumped out of the young man's hands. She shed her skin and became a beautiful girl. The young man took her hand and led her to the tent. And so they began to live. That's all.
